summary: T307 — extract the exact visa-desk hardening patterns that must be ported to trip assistance

findings.question: 1. The transition map — where it actually lives, verbatim text, and why it is "ONE map"
findings.answer:
⚠️ Path correction first: `src/lib/visa/visa-admin.ts` does NOT exist. The status machine is at **`/Users/mk1e3/eno-murat/src/lib/visa-admin.ts`** (217 lines; `src/lib/visa/` is the applicant-side layer: db.ts, records.ts, payments.ts, dm-*.ts …). The map is exactly where you expected, lines 157–164:

```ts
/** Legal admin transitions — MUST stay identical to the forum route's map. */
export const VISA_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS: Record<string, string[]> = {
  draft: ['cancelled'], ready_for_review: ['under_review', 'needs_changes', 'applicant_approval', 'cancelled'],
  under_review: ['needs_changes', 'applicant_approval', 'cancelled'], needs_changes: ['under_review', 'cancelled'],
  applicant_approval: ['under_review', 'needs_changes', 'cancelled'], ready_to_submit: ['applicant_approval', 'submitted', 'payment_required', 'processing', 'needs_changes', 'cancelled'],
  submitted: ['payment_required', 'processing', 'needs_changes', 'rejected', 'cancelled'], payment_required: ['submitted', 'processing', 'rejected', 'cancelled'],
  processing: ['approved', 'rejected', 'needs_changes', 'cancelled'], approved: [], rejected: [], cancelled: [],
}
```

Structure: a flat `Record<fromStatus, toStatus[]>` — an **outbound adjacency list**, keyed by the CURRENT status, values = the complete allow-list of next statuses. Terminal states are present with EXPLICIT empty arrays (`approved: [], rejected: [], cancelled: []`) rather than omitted, so "terminal" is data, not an absence.

What makes it ONE map rather than scattered checks: (a) it is the single `export`ed constant, consumed by both the enforcement point and the UI — the only validation in the applier is one membership test, `if (!(VISA_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS[app.status] || []).includes(next)) return { ok: false, error: 'invalid_status_transition' }` (`src/lib/visa-admin.ts:186`); there is no second `if (status === 'x' && next === 'y')` anywhere. (b) The button set is a SEPARATE presentation table, `VISA_ADMIN_ACTIONS` in `src/app/admin/visas/visa-status.ts:24-33`, whose doc comment binds it to the map — "Every pair MUST be legal under VISA_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS (the server re-validates regardless)" (`visa-status.ts:19-21`) — and the client component holds zero workflow knowledge: "the server computes which pairs apply from VISA_ADMIN_ACTIONS and passes them down — this component holds no workflow knowledge" (`src/app/admin/visas/[id]/case-actions.tsx:10-12`). (c) `|| []` on an unknown current status means the machine **fails closed**: an unrecognised status has no legal exits.

Caveat on "ONE": it is one map per app, DUPLICATED across the monorepo by hand. The forum route holds a byte-identical copy as a module-local `const transitions` (`apps/forum/src/app/api/visa/admin/applications/[id]/route.ts:15-21`), which is why line 157 says "MUST stay identical to the forum route's map". Nothing enforces that — no shared import, no test.

findings.question: 2. The applier and the compare-and-set on the PRIOR status — what call, what where-clause, what happens when the CAS loses, why a plain update is insufficient
findings.answer:
⚠️ **There is no Prisma here.** The visa tables are raw Postgres in the shared Supabase project, reached through **supabase-js / PostgREST** with the service-role client — not through Prisma (`src/lib/visa-admin.ts:2-11`: "plain postgres tables in the SAME Supabase project both apps share… over eno.vn's own service-role client"). `prisma/schema.prisma` has no visa_applications model; it only stores a `visaApplicationId String? @unique @db.Uuid` pointer on Conversation (`prisma/schema.prisma:604`).

The applier is `transitionVisaCase(id, next, admin)`, `src/lib/visa-admin.ts:178-216`. Order of operations:

1. `const db = visaDb(); if (!db) return { ok: false, error: 'visa_database_not_configured' }` (179-180) — env-absent is a soft state, not a throw.
2. Re-read the case: `const loaded = await loadVisaAdminCase(id)` → `unavailable` / `not-found` mapped to errors (181-183).
3. No-op short-circuit: `if (next === app.status) return { ok: true }` (185).
4. Map check (186), then the approve precondition: `if (next === 'approved' && !loaded.documents.some((item) => item.kind === 'result')) return { ok: false, error: 'result_document_required' }` (187-189).
5. The single write, whose where-clause IS the CAS (193, 205-207):

```ts
  }).eq('id', id).eq('status', app.status).select('id')
  if (error) return { ok: false, error: 'update_failed' }
  if (!data?.length) return { ok: false, error: 'case_changed_reload' }
```

So: **`db.from('visa_applications').update({...}).eq('id', id).eq('status', app.status).select('id')`** — a `UPDATE … WHERE id = $1 AND status = $2 RETURNING id`. The prior status read in step 2 is re-asserted in the WHERE clause, so validate-then-write is atomic at the row level. Loss detection is by **returned-row count**, which is why `.select('id')` is mandatory: without a RETURNING projection PostgREST hands back no rows and the code could not distinguish "0 rows matched" from success. `!data?.length` ⇒ the row moved under us ⇒ `case_changed_reload`, and NOTHING was written (no status, no timestamps, and — because the insert is downstream — no audit event).

Why a plain `.eq('id', id)` update is insufficient, in the code's own words at 202-204: "`.eq('status', …)` on top of the forum's id-only match: two operators (or this surface racing the forum one) can't double-apply a transition — the second write matches zero rows and reports stale instead of clobbering." Concretely, the gap between the read (181) and the write (193) is a real network round-trip against a table with **multiple independent writers**: the other admin surface (the forum PATCH route), the applicant's submit/cancel route (`src/app/api/visa/applications/[id]/submit/route.ts:45,76,101`), and the payment-capture handoff (`src/lib/visa/payments.ts:758-773`). Without the guard, an admin who validated `processing → approved` against a status the applicant has since cancelled would complete a transition that is illegal against the CURRENT row, and would overwrite `resolved_at`/`retention_until` set by that other writer.

Note a deliberate divergence from the forum: the forum CASes on **status AND updated_at** — `.eq('id', id).eq('status', app.status).eq('updated_at', app.updated_at).select('*').maybeSingle()` (`apps/forum/…/route.ts:73`, with the rationale at 69-72), because that handler re-encrypts a payload it decrypted from the stale read. eno.vn's version is status-only because it is status-only by design and leaves `encrypted_payload` byte-identical (`src/lib/visa-admin.ts:172-176`). The applicant-side writers in this repo all use the stronger status+updated_at form (`submit/route.ts:89,101`; `payments.ts:773`).

findings.question: 3. Timestamp stamping, audit-event append, and transactionality — what exactly goes into the event row
4. The full status set and the complete legal-transition map
findings.answer:
The status vocabulary is a 12-value tuple, `src/lib/visa/schema.ts:160`:

```ts
export const visaStatuses = ['draft', 'ready_for_review', 'under_review', 'needs_changes', 'applicant_approval', 'ready_to_submit', 'submitted', 'payment_required', 'processing', 'approved', 'rejected', 'cancelled'] as const
```

(byte-identical copy at `apps/forum/src/lib/visa/schema.ts:166`; the forum route zod-validates input against it, `apps/forum/…/route.ts:12`.)

ADMIN-legal edges, in full (`src/lib/visa-admin.ts:158-164`):

- draft → cancelled
- ready_for_review → under_review, needs_changes, applicant_approval, cancelled
- under_review → needs_changes, applicant_approval, cancelled
- needs_changes → under_review, cancelled
- applicant_approval → under_review, needs_changes, cancelled
- ready_to_submit → applicant_approval, submitted, payment_required, processing, needs_changes, cancelled
- submitted → payment_required, processing, needs_changes, rejected, cancelled
- payment_required → submitted, processing, rejected, cancelled
- processing → approved, rejected, needs_changes, cancelled
- approved → (none) · rejected → (none) · cancelled → (none)

Structural facts: `cancelled` is reachable from every non-terminal state; `approved` is reachable ONLY from `processing`, and only with a `kind === 'result'` document present (`:187-189`); `rejected` only from submitted / payment_required / processing. **`ready_for_review` and `ready_to_submit` have NO inbound admin edge** — the desk can never move a case into them. Those two are written exclusively by applicant/payment paths: `ready_for_review` by the applicant's send_for_review (`src/app/api/visa/applications/[id]/submit/route.ts:76`) or the capture handoff (`src/lib/visa/payments.ts:759`), `ready_to_submit` by the applicant's approve action (`submit/route.ts:101`); `draft` only at creation (`src/app/api/visa/applications/route.ts:257`, `src/lib/visa/dm-flow.ts:1159`); and the applicant can self-cancel from any non-terminal state (`submit/route.ts:42-45`). The map is therefore the ADMIN half of a larger machine, not the whole machine.

The operator-visible subset is narrower still — `VISA_ADMIN_ACTIONS` (`src/app/admin/visas/visa-status.ts:24-33`) exposes no `cancelled` button anywhere and no `draft` row, e.g. `processing: [['approved','Approve'], ['needs_changes','Action required'], ['rejected','Reject']]`. Legal-but-unexposed ≠ illegal: the server allows any mapped edge that reaches it.

findings.question: 5. Is there a test for the status machine?
findings.answer:
**No. The admin status machine is entirely untested.** I searched every test file in the repo: `grep -rln 'VISA_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS|transitionVisaCase|transitionVisaStatus|VISA_ADMIN_ACTIONS'` returns only four non-test files (`src/lib/visa-admin.ts`, `src/app/admin/visas/visa-status.ts`, `src/app/admin/visas/[id]/actions.ts`, `src/app/admin/visas/[id]/case-actions.tsx`), and `case_changed_reload` / `invalid_status_transition` appear in no test at all. The three test files that mock `@/lib/visa-admin` mock it only for constants/types (`src/lib/visa/result.test.ts:96` → `vi.mock('@/lib/visa-admin', () => ({ VISA_BUCKET: 'visa-documents' }))`; `src/lib/visa/bundle.test.ts:63`). `apps/forum` contains no `*.test.ts` files whatsoever, so the source map has no test either.

The two nearest things, useful as templates for the test you should write:

1. **`src/lib/visa/payments.capture-guard.test.ts`** — the closest analogue, and it tests the same hardening concerns on the APPLICANT handoff, not on the admin machine. Its cases: `'MISMATCH: the payment stamps, the handoff is withheld, the desk gets a named event'` (:195), `'an unreadable audit trail fails CLOSED — the handoff waits until it can be verified'` (:215), and a whole describe block `'the atomic capture (visa_capture_payment RPC) — race + idempotency outcomes'` (:239) asserting `'app_gone: a delete lands BETWEEN the read and the atomic flip → not_found, no paid record'` (:292) and `'unexpected: a shaky checkout row → the tx ROLLS BACK (throws, app NOT stamped paid)'` (:304). Its header comment (:16) even documents the queue's `.or('status.neq.draft,paid_at.not.is.null')` read from visa-admin.ts — so the queue filter is asserted, the transition applier is not.
2. **`e2e/admin/dashboard-rail.spec.ts:47-50`** — `'/admin/visas responds for the admin with the visa queue'`, a 200-status smoke test only. It exercises no transition.

One adjacent unit test does assert a boundary of the machine from outside: `src/lib/visa/result.test.ts:541`, `'does not change the case status — approval stays a separate, gated transition'` — i.e. uploading the result PDF must not itself flip the status (the invariant restated at `case-actions.tsx:124-126`).

gotchas: WRONG PATH / WRONG ORM in the premise. The file is `src/lib/visa-admin.ts`, not `src/lib/visa/visa-admin.ts`, and there is **no Prisma call anywhere in it** — it is supabase-js/PostgREST against the shared Supabase project with a service-role client (`src/lib/visa-admin.ts:2-11`, `visaDb()` at :70-74). If you port this to a Prisma-backed trip-assistance table, the CAS must be rewritten: `prisma.trip.updateMany({ where: { id, status: prior }, data: {...} })` and check `count === 0`. Do NOT reach for `prisma.trip.update({ where: { id } })` — a unique-`where` update cannot express the status predicate and will happily clobber.

`.select('id')` IS the loss detector, not decoration. Loss is inferred from `!data?.length` (`:207`). Drop the RETURNING projection (or switch to `.maybeSingle()` without noticing it returns `null` on 0 rows AND on error) and a lost CAS silently reads as success — the worst possible failure for a status machine. With Prisma the equivalent is `updateMany().count`; with `update()` you get a thrown P2025 instead, which is a different control flow.

The update is a full READ-MODIFY-WRITE, not a patch. Every untouched column is re-sent with the value read one round-trip earlier (`authorized_at: authorizationRefresh ? null : app.authorized_at`, `submitted_at: … : app.submitted_at`, `retention_until: … : app.retention_until` — `:195-200`). That is exactly why the CAS is load-bearing: without it, a concurrent writer's changes to those columns are overwritten with stale values even when the status happens to agree. If your port sends only the changed fields, you have changed the concurrency semantics and the status-only CAS may no longer be sufficient.

STATUS-ONLY CAS IS THE WEAKER OF THE TWO VARIANTS IN THIS REPO — do not copy it blindly. Every writer that stamps a hash or re-encrypts a payload CASes on status **AND** updated_at: `apps/forum/.../route.ts:73` (rationale at :69-72 — "this update RE-ENCRYPTS a payload decrypted from the read above"), `src/app/api/visa/applications/[id]/submit/route.ts:89,101`, `src/lib/visa/payments.ts:773`. visa-admin.ts gets away with status-only precisely because it writes no derived-from-stale-read content (`:172-176`: "`encrypted_payload` is left byte-identical"). The moment your trip-assistance transition also writes a snapshot/hash/derived blob, you MUST add `.eq('updated_at', prior.updated_at)` or your CAS is a false sense of safety: two admins going `A→B` and `A→B` with different derived content both match `status = 'A'`.

THE AUDIT EVENT CAN VANISH. It is a second network call after the commit, and its `error` is never read — the function returns `{ ok: true }` regardless (`:211-215`). That is a deliberate trade (the comment at :209-210: failing it "must not tell the operator the transition failed… and bait a re-click into invalid_status_transition"), but it means the event log is NOT a reliable ledger. Contrast `recordVisaEvent`, which throws (`src/lib/visa/records.ts:44`). If your trip feature needs a provable audit trail (money, refunds, liability), copy the RPC pattern instead — `db.rpc('visa_capture_payment', …)` (`src/lib/visa/payments.ts:626`, DDL `scripts/visa-capture-payment-fn.mjs:56`) puts the event insert inside the transaction so "it commits with the money or rolls back".

`if (next === app.status) return { ok: true }` (:185) silently no-ops. Idempotent for a double-click, but note the forum handler does NOT early-return — it writes and records a `case_details_updated` event (`apps/forum/.../route.ts:76`), because there it also carries field edits. If your ported transition ever carries a payload alongside the status, this early return will DROP those edits whenever the status is unchanged.

`resolved_at: final ? now.toISOString() : null` (:199) unconditionally NULLS resolved_at on every non-final transition — unlike `retention_until` and `submitted_at`, which preserve the prior value. It is currently harmless only because every state that can hold a `resolved_at` is terminal with zero outgoing edges. If your trip machine allows any exit from a resolved/terminal state (reopen, un-cancel, appeal), copying this line silently erases the resolution timestamp. Also note the 90-day retention here vs 30 days on the applicant cancel path (`src/app/api/visa/applications/[id]/submit/route.ts:45`) — the two are inconsistent by hand; pick one deliberately.

THE MAP IS ONLY THE ADMIN HALF. `ready_for_review` and `ready_to_submit` have no inbound admin edge, and four other code paths write `status` outside this map: applicant send_for_review and approve (`submit/route.ts:76,101`), applicant self-cancel (`submit/route.ts:45` — which has NO CAS at all, just `.eq('id', id)`), the payment-capture handoff (`payments.ts:759`), and creation (`route.ts:257`, `dm-flow.ts:1159`). Auditing only `VISA_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS` and concluding "these are the legal transitions" is wrong — the real machine is the union of all writers, and the CAS exists BECAUSE of the writers not in the map.

There is a HIDDEN DUPLICATE that nothing keeps in sync. `apps/forum/src/app/api/visa/admin/applications/[id]/route.ts:15-21` holds a byte-identical `transitions` const, and `src/app/admin/visas/visa-status.ts:24-33` holds the button table that must be a subset. Three copies, one comment saying "MUST stay identical" (:157), zero tests and zero shared import. Do not add a fourth copy for trips — export one map and derive the UI from it. (Note also `src/lib/sync-pairs.test.ts` byte-couples six `src/lib/visa/*` files to their forum twins; visa-admin.ts is NOT one of them, so it is safe to edit, but any new logic you put in a sync-paired file will fail the root vitest suite.)

`next` is never validated against the status vocabulary. `transitionVisaCase(id, next: string, …)` takes a raw string straight from a client-invoked server action (`src/app/admin/visas/[id]/actions.ts:12-15`); the only thing stopping garbage is the allow-list membership test. That is safe (allow-list, and `|| []` fails closed on an unknown current status), but it means an off-by-one typo in a map key produces a permanently dead-end state rather than a type error. The forum side zod-validates against `visaStatuses` (`apps/forum/.../route.ts:12`) — worth keeping in the port; consider typing the map as `Record<TripStatus, TripStatus[]>` so a bad key fails at `tsc`.

On CAS loss the UI shows a toast but does not re-render. `case-actions.tsx:31-35` fires `toast.error('Update failed: case changed reload')` and neither calls `router.refresh()` nor revalidates (the server action only revalidates on `result.ok` — `actions.ts:16-19`). The operator is left staring at the stale action set that just lost the race and can click it again. Fix this in the port: refresh on the stale-conflict error specifically.

Fail-soft vs fail-loud is a deliberate, narrow contract — do not widen it. Only `42P01`/`PGRST205` degrade to "unavailable" (`:62-68`), and the comment is explicit: "any other error is a real failure and must surface, not read as an empty queue". Likewise `visaDb()` swallows only the env-absent throw from `getSupabaseAdmin()` (:70-74). A port that wraps the whole thing in a generic try/catch turns a broken DB into an empty, apparently-healthy queue.

Two preconditions are easy to leave behind because they are not in the map: the approve gate requires a `kind === 'result'` document (`:187-189` — evidence, not status, is what unlocks the terminal state), and `assigned_admin: app.assigned_admin || admin` (:194) is claim-once, never re-assign. Also, the whole surface deliberately cannot touch encrypted payload fields because `VISA_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is absent from eno.vn (:13-20) — "never ship a copy of the crypto without its key."

Ship a test with the port; the original has none. Minimum table-driven set: every legal edge accepted; a representative illegal edge → `invalid_status_transition`; unknown current status → no legal exits; `next === current` → ok with zero writes; approve without the result doc → refused; CAS-loss (mock 0 returned rows) → `case_changed_reload` AND no event inserted; event-insert failure → still `{ ok: true }`; `submitted_at` not re-stamped on a second pass. `src/lib/visa/payments.capture-guard.test.ts` is the in-repo model for mocking the supabase chain.

findings.question: 1. How is the SENDER resolved from the desk owner, and why must it never come from an argument? (dm-thread.ts:30-33)
2. What ownership is proven before binding, and against what? (dm-thread.ts:34-37)
3. How is "mode" DERIVED from the newest matching event with no column? Show the query/sort and the tie-breaking. (dm-thread.ts:73-85)
4. Why is this file "the ONLY file that authors a card"? What breaks if another file writes one?
findings.answer:
The file states its own reason at :21-27:

```
// One module owns the relationship between a visa case (a row in Supabase's
// visa_applications, outside Prisma's datamodel) and the marketplace conversation that
// case is lived out in. Everything that writes a card, binds a thread, or asks who is
// driving the conversation goes through here, so the four spoofing gates documented in
// src/lib/messages.ts have exactly one authoring surface above them.
```

The invariants are split across two layers, and only the lower one is structurally enforced. messages.ts's `buildCardMeta` (:250-293) holds four gates that fire on EVERY card write no matter who calls: (1) `if (!convo.sellerProfileId || convo.sellerProfileId !== senderId) throw new Error('visa_card_author_forbidden')` (:252); (4) strict zod `metaSchemaFor(kind).safeParse(meta)` → `visa_card_meta_invalid` (:254-255); (2) the binding proof — immutable `visa_applications.conversation_id` is authoritative when non-null, live `Conversation.visaApplicationId` only as fallback, else `visa_card_application_mismatch` (:277-286) — re-asserted under a row lock inside the insert transaction (:356-363); (3) `if (kind === 'visa_checkout' && (data as VisaCheckoutMeta).status === 'paid') throw new Error('visa_checkout_paid_not_authorable')` (:289).

What dm-thread.ts adds on TOP, which nothing below enforces:

- Sender resolution from the storefront (Q1) — messages.ts only *compares* a senderId; it cannot invent the right one.
- The pre-flight `convo.visaApplicationId !== applicationId` and `convo.sellerProfileId !== senderId` checks (:349-352, :404-405, :472) that turn a would-be throw into a `null`.
- The refusal CONTRACT: "Returns null — never throws — when the shop, the binding, or the thread's mode makes emission illegal, so a stalled wizard degrades to 'no card' instead of a 500 in the middle of a chat" (:323-327). Each function try/catches insertMessage (:373-381, :411-422, :480-491).
- The mode gate — the wizard not talking over a human (:354-364). This exists ONLY here; messages.ts knows nothing about modes.
- Empty body + constant PII-free preview: `insertMessage(convo, senderId, '', { kind: 'visa_step', meta, preview: visaDmStepPreview(step) })` (:376). Body must be empty or the realtime broadcast renders a plain text bubble (messages.ts:302-306), and `preview` lands in the plaintext `Conversation.lastMessageText` both inboxes read (messages.ts:209-215) — hence "⚠️ NO PII" at :60-61.
- The money normalization for checkout: shape validation and writing the NORMALIZED value (:454-465).
- `needsReview` sanitizing so one bad key costs that key, not the card: `[...new Set(input.needsReview ?? [])].filter(isVisaPayloadFieldName).slice(0, 80)` (:366-368).

So a foreign writer that calls insertMessage directly would still be blocked from spoofing an author, naming another case, or minting 'paid' — the gates hold. What it WOULD break: it could post over a human admin (no mode gate); it could 500 a chat mid-wizard instead of degrading (no null contract); it could leak applicant data into `lastMessageText`, or render a stray text bubble by passing a non-empty body; it could write a sub-cent or client-supplied price; and one stray needsReview key would throw away the whole card. It would also need `visaApplicationId` in its select — `ConvoForSend` marks it optional precisely so ordinary send routes cannot author cards (messages.ts:195-200: "Callers that don't select it simply cannot author cards, which is why the ordinary send routes are safe untouched"), which is what `THREAD_SELECT` (:65-68) supplies.

⚠️ Factual correction for the port: this file is not literally the only authoring surface any more. `src/lib/visa/result.ts:287-315` (`sendVisaResultCard`) authors the fourth card kind, `visa_result`, itself — and it re-implements the same discipline rather than importing it: `const shop = await getVisaShopSeller(); if (!shop?.ownerId) return null; const senderId = shop.ownerId`, then `if (!convo || convo.sellerProfileId !== senderId) return null`, empty body + bilingual preview, null-never-throw (:316-324), and NO mode gate on purpose (:278-280). `MESSAGE_KINDS`/`VisaCardKind` in messages.ts:28-31 list all four. The accurate rule is: dm-thread.ts is the only authoring surface for visa_step / visa_picker / visa_checkout, and result.ts is a deliberate second one for visa_result that copies the contract verbatim.

findings.question: 5. How is the Conversation resolved/created? The listingId + buyerProfileId uniqueness handling, and what happens on a race.

gotchas: dm-thread.ts is NOT literally the only card author, despite the header's claim. src/lib/visa/result.ts:287-315 authors the fourth kind (visa_result) with its own copy of the sender/thread/preview discipline and no mode gate (result.ts:278-280). MESSAGE_KINDS at src/lib/messages.ts:28 lists all four: 'visa_step','visa_checkout','visa_result','visa_picker'. A port that centralizes only the three dm-thread kinds will silently drop visa_result — or, worse, a port that 'consolidates' result.ts into dm-thread must keep its distinct thread resolution (resolveVisaResultThread) and its unique-index race decider (result.ts:316-324, partial unique index message_one_result_card_per_document — the loser returning null is what makes the thank-you email exactly-once).

Never add a sender/actor parameter to any of these functions, and never 'improve' them by accepting the session profile as the author. dm-thread.ts:30-33 and :337-342 are explicit: the resolution from getVisaShopSeller().ownerId is what bounds the damage of a mis-authorized call. Equally: these functions take NO ACTOR and are NOT entitlement checks (:42-49) — the ROUTE must authenticate and prove the actor is the applicant or a visa admin before calling sendVisaStepCard / sendVisaCheckoutCard / setVisaThreadMode / markVisaThreadPaid. bindVisaThread is the ONE self-gating exception (:55-57).

visaConversationIdFor THROWS on lookup error and returns null ONLY for a genuine 'no link' (:98-112). Do not port it as null-on-error 'for robustness' — the file records this as an external-review fix: collapsing error into null would make a transient Supabase blip either silently refuse a legitimate card or misroute a finished visa to the wrong thread and undo the upload. Its two consumers depend on the distinction (messages.ts:277-286 binding proof; findVisaThreadByCase's fallback).

The immutable/live binding precedence is asymmetric and the insert-time lock predicate DEPENDS on which proof was used. messages.ts:356-358: immutable proof locks by `{ id: convo.id }` alone; live proof keeps `{ id, visaApplicationId }`. Re-asserting the live pointer under an immutable proof IS the stranding bug (a rebound thread matches 0 rows and refuses a legitimate card for an earlier case). Port `proof` through, not just the boolean 'is it bound'.

A non-null conversation_id that resolves to no usable desk thread returns null — it must NOT fall through to the live binding (findVisaThreadByCase, :296-321). 'A link that points nowhere is corrupt state, not a signal to try the very pointer the link exists to replace.' The fallback is reserved strictly for a NULL link.

Two mode readers with deliberately OPPOSITE failure contracts, and picking the wrong one is a user-visible bug. getVisaThreadMode fails soft to 'ai' (correct for step/picker cards — furniture must not wedge the wizard); readVisaThreadModeStrict returns { ok:false } (required for the Eno concierge, which is a VOICE — owner rule 'ife person requested ai doesnt answer'). :644-657 records that an adversarial review caught the concierge consuming the soft value. Do not collapse them into one function with a flag.

'human_requested' does NOT silence the wizard — only 'admin' does (:354-356). And `byAdmin` is a real exception that must survive the port (owner-requested: 'admin can send visa application form from chip'), settable ONLY by the resend path after proving the caller is the desk. sendVisaCheckoutCard has NO mode gate at all, on purpose (:477-478).

MODE_EVENT_NAMES is derived from MODE_FOR_EVENT (`Object.keys`, :86), so the two maps must stay in sync or the `.in('event', …)` filter and the reverse mapping drift apart. The tie-break `.order('id',{ascending:false})` is DETERMINISTIC but not chronological: recordVisaEvent inserts `id: crypto.randomUUID()` (src/lib/visa/records.ts:43), so same-created_at events resolve by random-uuid order — stable, arbitrary. Don't port it as if uuid desc meant 'later'.

Mode WRITES throw, mode READS don't (:680-689). setVisaThreadMode is the file's one loud path — a takeover the caller believes landed but didn't leaves the wizard posting over a human. recordVisaEvent throws on any PostgREST error (records.ts:44). Don't wrap setVisaThreadMode in a swallowing try/catch.

Cards must be inserted with an EMPTY body and a constant PII-free `preview`. A non-empty body is appended as a plain text bubble until the 15s backstop poll (the realtime broadcast carries only id/senderProfileId/body/createdAt — messages.ts:302-306), and `preview` lands in the plaintext Conversation.lastMessageText both inboxes read (messages.ts:209-215). '⚠️ NO PII' (:60-61) covers body, metaJson AND lastMessageText.

Money: sendVisaCheckoutCard validates SHAPE ONLY, never value — pricing is per-product since 2026-07-21 and visaPaymentsConfig().feeCents 'is NOT the price of anything this card sells' (:429-437). The card is written from the NORMALIZED `cents / 100`, not the raw input, and Math.round absorbs float noise while the 1e-6 epsilon still refuses 25.999 (:458-465). ⚠️ 'A CLIENT-SUPPLIED AMOUNT MUST NEVER REACH THIS FUNCTION' — a route forwarding body.amountUsd is a price-tampering hole this layer cannot close (:439-441).

'paid' is never authorable and has TWO writers that each re-assert the evidence gate independently. Canonical: setVisaCheckoutStatus (messages.ts, requires the live binding). Second: stampReleasedVisaCheckoutCard (:559-581) for a case whose thread was rebound — without it a repeat applicant's first case keeps an 'unpaid' card forever for a real capture. Both require visa_applications.paid_at to already exist. The second writer also round-trips the merged blob through parseMessageMeta BEFORE writing (:572-579) — an external review caught it as the only metaJson writer that skipped the strict parse. markVisaThreadPaid must NEVER throw (a payment is already recorded; a 500 makes Stripe retry a completed capture) — :594-615.

findVisaCheckoutCardByApplication FAILS CLOSED ON AMBIGUITY: if the case's cards appear in more than one thread it refuses to stamp (:535-538). Its cross-tenant guard is the SCOPING itself — `{ sellerId: shop.id, buyerProfileId: ownerProfileId }` with take:20/take:50 — 'a card living in anyone else's thread is invisible here, whatever its metaJson claims'. Don't 'optimize' it into a global message scan by metaJson.

The reuse lookup is by (sellerId, buyerProfileId) but the DB constraint is @@unique([listingId, buyerProfileId]) (prisma/schema.prisma:607). The P2002 catch re-queries by SELLER, not by listing (:226-230). Keep both shapes as-is; matching the catch to the constraint's key would find a different (or no) row. Any non-P2002 error must re-throw, and 'no raced winner' must be thread_conflict, never a fabricated thread.

Rebinding is unbind-then-claim inside ONE transaction, with `claim.count !== 1` as the concurrency verdict (:237-254). Two conditional updateMany calls, not an unconditional update — splitting them across transactions lets a concurrent card write land against a half-moved binding. Cards from the released case must stay in the timeline; every renderer treats meta.applicationId ≠ Conversation.visaApplicationId as inert HISTORY (:241-244, schema :600-603). Deleting old cards on rebind would be wrong.

stampVisaConversationId is write-once BY PREDICATE (`.is('conversation_id', null)`), not by a DB trigger, and it is fail-soft by contract — a failed stamp is logged and swallowed so it can never fail a committed bind (:118-139). Two consequences to carry over: treat the column as append-only by convention (any other service-role query could still overwrite it), and a bind whose stamp failed leaves the case on the live-binding fallback until the next attempt. Also note it is called on BOTH success paths — including the already-bound early return (:198), which is how legacy cases get healed.

THREAD_SELECT (:65-68) is load-bearing, not a convenience: `visaApplicationId` is optional on messages.ts's ConvoForSend precisely so ordinary send routes CANNOT author cards (messages.ts:195-200). A port that widens the conversation select globally, or makes visaApplicationId required, removes that structural barrier.

needsReview is filtered, deduped and capped — `[...new Set(...)].filter(isVisaPayloadFieldName).slice(0, 80)` (:366-368) — so one stray key costs that key rather than the whole card (the strict parse in messages.ts would throw). It carries payload FIELD NAMES only; there is no free-text channel in a card blob by design (messages.ts gate 4).

This file uses RELATIVE import specifiers on purpose (:2-4): `@/…` does not resolve under vitest and every branch here is unit-tested (dm-thread.test.ts). Also: messages.ts imports visaConversationIdFor via a LAZY `await import('@/lib/visa/dm-thread')` (messages.ts:277) specifically to break the dm-thread↔messages cycle. A port that converts either to a static top-level import can reintroduce the cycle or break the vitest suite.

Repo constraint before touching neighbours: src/lib/sync-pairs.test.ts byte-couples six src/lib/visa/* files (mrz, image-quality, image-normalization, checkpoints, schema, crypto) to their apps/forum copies — dm-thread.ts is NOT in that list, but schema.ts (which isVisaPayloadFieldName/the payload field names come from) IS. Editing a paired file fails the root vitest suite until the pair is mirrored.

findings.question: 1. dm-flow.ts :68-72 — the rule that NO amount may come from a request body. Where does the amount come from instead, and who types it?
2. visa-shop.ts around :66 — the "plural env" resolver. What env var(s), why PLURAL, and what production incident does the comment record?
findings.answer:
Two constants: the singular `VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAIL` (visa-shop.ts:61) and the plural resolver `VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAILS` (visa-shop.ts:84-89). BOTH read the SAME single env var `process.env.VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAIL`; the plural one comma-splits it. There is no `VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAILS` env var.

```
export const VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAIL = (process.env.VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAIL || 'support@eno.forum').trim().toLowerCase()   // :61

export const VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAILS: readonly string[] = (
  process.env.VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAIL || 'support@eno.forum'
)
  .split(',')
  .map((e) => e.trim().toLowerCase())
  .filter(Boolean)                                                                                                   // :84-89
```

The comment at :63-83, verbatim on the key lines:

```
 * ⚠️ A LIST, because pinning ONE address silently disabled the whole visa surface in prod.
 *
 * Found 2026-07-22: VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAIL is set in NEITHER the local env nor the deployed
 * secret, so it fell back to 'support@eno.vn' — for which no Profile row exists. The six
 * live e-visa products are owned by 'support@eno.forum'. getVisaShopSeller() therefore
 * matched nothing and every card, binding and charge path failed closed, while the products
 * sat published on the marketplace.
```

The incident: 2026-07-22, the constant's own FALLBACK named the pre-migration address `support@eno.vn`, for which no Profile exists (the account consolidation moved auth.users.email AND Profile.email to `support@eno.forum`). `getVisaShopSeller()` matched nothing → every card, thread binding and charge path failed closed while products stayed published. Corrected note at :72-83 adds that an earlier version of this comment had the direction backwards, and that `support@eno.vn` is a Cloudflare mail REDIRECT into support@eno.forum, never an account — so it is deliberately NOT in the list ("keeping it here would have kept a dead identity alive as a live one"). It stays plural because the failure mode (one pinned address takes the whole surface down silently) is real. Consumed at visa-shop.ts:250-252: `where: { owner: { email: { in: [...VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAILS] } } }` — `in`, not `equals`, ordered `memberSince: 'asc'` so a duplicated identity resolves deterministically to the ORIGINAL storefront holding the live products.

findings.question: 3. Where is the visa desk's listing/seller resolved, and how is a missing one handled — fail open or closed?
findings.answer:
SELLER: `getVisaShopSeller()` — visa-shop.ts:245-260, a React `cache()`d per-request lookup resolved BY OWNER EMAIL (never a hardcoded seller id): `db.seller.findFirst({ where: { owner: { email: { in: [...VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAILS] } } }, orderBy: { memberSince: 'asc' } })`, wrapped in try/catch that logs and `return null` (:256-259).

LISTINGS: `getVisaShopListings()` (visa-shop.ts:331-365) — `if (!seller) return []`, scoped `where: { sellerId: seller.id }`, `take: 200`, catch → `[]`. "MEMBERSHIP IS THE STOREFRONT, not a marker string" (:325-329) — filtering on `externalId` would hide admin-uploaded products. Then `getVisaShopProductsForSale()` (:368-369, verified && status==='active'), `getVisaShopProducts()` (:412-433, drops rows whose price is not sellable), and `resolveVisaProduct()` (:443-446) — "⚠️ THIS IS THE PRICE. A client may name WHICH listing it wants; the amount comes from here and from nowhere else. Resolved by re-reading the catalogue rather than by its own query, so a product can never be chargeable through this function under rules the shop page did not apply" (:436-442). The hidden $0 generic anchor is looked up separately by externalId over the RAW list (`findVisaGenericAnchor`, :506-508) precisely so it "can never be resolved as a product, never be charged".

MISSING = FAIL CLOSED at every consumer; the LOOKUP is fail-soft (null/[]) only so a surface renders "no products yet" instead of a 500 (:43-46). Every money/card path turns that null into a refusal:
- dm-flow.ts:1085-1086 `const shop = await getVisaShopSeller(); if (!shop?.ownerId) return fail('shop_unavailable', 503)` — checked BEFORE a case is created ("an application minted against a desk that cannot answer is an orphan").
- dm-flow.ts:837-838 (resend) `if (!shop?.ownerId || shop.ownerId !== thread.sellerProfileId) return fail('shop_unavailable', 503)` — also proves the thread's seller seat IS the desk.
- dm-thread.ts:166-168 `if (!shop?.ownerId) return { ok: false, error: 'shop_unavailable' }` (bindVisaThread); dm-thread.ts:343, :398, :467 (sendVisaCheckoutCard), :512 all `return null` → no card, and dm-flow turns null into `step_card_refused` / `checkout_card_refused` 503 (dm-flow.ts:704, :740).
- concierge.ts:411-412 and result.ts:293-294 same pattern (503 / null).
- Checkout: no seller ⇒ `getVisaShopListings()` = [] ⇒ `resolveVisaProduct` null ⇒ 409 `product_price_unavailable`/`listing_not_found` (checkout route.ts:174-179 + explainUnsellable :89-110). explainUnsellable even documents that a failed DB probe "must refuse the charge rather than guess a price".
No path substitutes a default seller, a default listing or a default price.

findings.question: 4. prisma/schema.prisma :636-640 — the metaJson comment/field. What is allowed, what is explicitly forbidden?
5. Does ANY visa code path accept a client-supplied price, fee or amount? Proof either way.
findings.answer:
NO. Every visa POST body is a zod `.strict()` object with no money field, so an amount is a loud 400 rather than a silently-ignored key:
- start: `z.object({ listingId: z.string().trim().min(1).max(64).optional() }).strict()` — start/route.ts:39-43, with the rule at :27-30 ("THE CLIENT NAMES A PRODUCT, NEVER A PRICE… a client that starts sending an amount gets a loud 400").
- select-product: `z.object({ listingId: z.string().trim().min(1).max(64) }).strict()` — select-product/route.ts:31-33 (rule :18-21). Proven by test: select-product/route.test.ts:70 `expect((await post({ listingId: 'listing-1', amountUsd: 1 })).status).toBe(400) // .strict()`.
- card act: `z.object({ action: z.enum(['acknowledge','skip','edit']), fields: z.record(z.string().max(64), z.string().max(1200)).optional() }).strict()` — act/route.ts:39-45. `fields` is further narrowed by the step allowlist (dm-flow.ts applyVisaDmFieldEdit :576-585, "THE STEP IS THE ALLOWLIST") and no step owns a price field.
- advance / resend: no body at all; resend copies the amount off the live card and never re-quotes (dm-flow.ts:808-812, :874-886).
- PATCH application: `z.object({ payload: visaPayloadSchema })` — applications/[id]/route.ts:17. visaPayloadSchema has exactly one numeric money-ish field, `estimatedExpenses` (visa/schema.ts:61) — a government-form trip-budget declaration, referenced nowhere in any pricing/charging path.
- checkout (the only route that charges): bodySchema is `{ provider, listingId, declarationAccepted, prefillAuthorized, quote? }.strict()` — checkout/route.ts:65-81. Both client-supplied identifiers are CONFIRMATION TOKENS, compared and never used:
  · listingId: `const canonicalListingId = storedSelection || (await selectedVisaDmListingId(id))` (:158-159); `if (!canonicalListingId) return … 'product_not_selected' 409` ("Fail closed rather than let the body choose", :160); `if (parsed.data.listingId !== canonicalListingId) return … 'listing_selection_mismatch' 409` (:166-171); the product is then `await resolveVisaProduct(canonicalListingId)` with the comment "Resolved from the CANONICAL listing id, never parsed.data.listingId" (:174-176).
  · quote: parsed by `parseVisaQuote`, then only `isQuoteChargeable` / `visaQuoteDrifted` comparisons → 409 `quote_expired` / `quote_changed` (:266-278), with the note "It is compared, never used" and "this can NEVER cheapen the charge".
  · The charge line, checkout/route.ts:280-283: `// ⚠️ THE LINE THAT DECIDES THE CHARGED AMOUNT. It reads exactly one thing: the quote / // this request just issued from the admin's đồng price. Not the body, not the echo, / // not a config, not a cached catalogue number.` then `const amountCents = quote.amountUsdCents`. A defence-in-depth re-assert sits just above at :209-210 (`!Number.isSafeInteger(product.priceVnd) || product.priceVnd <= 0 || product.currency !== 'VND'` → 409).
- payment confirm: body is only `{ provider, ref }` (confirm/route.ts:19-22) — no amount. The amount is read from the PROVIDER (`stripeRetrieveSession` / `paypalCaptureOrder`, :53-55) and then compared against OUR row: payments.ts:607 `if (input.amountCents < paymentRow.amount_cents || input.currency.toUpperCase() !== paymentRow.currency.toUpperCase()) return { ok:false, error:'amount_mismatch' }`, where `visa_payments.amount_cents` was written server-side at checkout (checkout/route.ts:303-311).
- Stripe webhook: HMAC over the raw body is the auth (payments/stripe/webhook/route.ts:21-22) and the amount comes from `session.amount_total` (:43), still subject to the same amount_mismatch comparison.
The only genuine crack is architectural, not a live hole: `sendVisaCheckoutCard` TAKES an `amountUsd` argument and cannot tell where it came from — dm-thread.ts:439-441 "⚠️ A CLIENT-SUPPLIED AMOUNT MUST NEVER REACH THIS FUNCTION… a route that forwards `body.amountUsd` is a price-tampering hole this layer cannot close for it." Its only two callers are dm-flow's server price chain (dm-flow.ts:739) and the copy-the-live-card resend (dm-flow.ts:887). Its own gates are shape-only: positive whole-cent (dm-thread.ts:460-465) plus the messages.ts:122 metaJson backstop.

gotchas: `sendVisaCheckoutCard(input.amountUsd)` is the one function that cannot enforce the invariant itself (dm-thread.ts:439-441). Its checks are SHAPE only (finite, positive, whole-cent — dm-thread.ts:460-465) plus the metaJson backstop (messages.ts:122). If a port ever forwards a request-body amount into it, every gate downstream still passes. Keep its callers to exactly two: the server price chain (dm-flow.ts:739) and the copy-from-live-card resend (dm-flow.ts:887).

ADVANCE RE-QUOTES, RESEND COPIES — and the asymmetry is deliberate. advanceVisaDmFlow supersedes a card whose amount no longer matches a fresh quote (dm-flow.ts:718-722, :735-739); resendVisaDmCard reuses `existing?.meta.amountUsd` and only falls back to the price chain when there is NO card at all (dm-flow.ts:874-886, doc at :808-812). Making resend re-quote would put a number in front of the buyer that the desk never showed; making advance copy would dead-end the buyer against the checkout route's drift refusal.

The checkout body's `listingId` and `quote` are CONFIRMATION TOKENS, compared for equality and then discarded. The product is resolved from the case's canonical selection (checkout/route.ts:158-176) and the amount from the freshly issued quote (:283). Using `parsed.data.listingId` to resolve the product, or `shown` as the amount, is the price-tampering hole. Note the echo is OPTIONAL — an absent quote is legal and must not be treated as a failure (:264-265).

VISA_SHOP_OWNER_EMAIL must stay comma-splittable AND its fallback must stay 'support@eno.forum' (visa-shop.ts:61, :84-89). Pinning one address, or restoring the 'support@eno.vn' fallback, silently killed the ENTIRE visa surface in prod on 2026-07-22 — products published, every card/binding/charge failing closed. ⚠️ The root CLAUDE.md still asserts the visa admin identity is `support@eno.vn`; the CODE and its verified-in-DB comment say otherwise. Do not 'fix' the code to match the doc. support@eno.vn is a Cloudflare mail redirect, never an account.

The currency gate must stay pointed at ₫: `sellablePriceVnd` accepts only '₫' | 'Đ' | 'VND' and refuses '$' rather than converting (visa-shop.ts:217-225). A short-lived earlier rule stored visa prices in '$' and this file refused everything else (f7f8ca40) — reading ₫3.000.000 as dollars is a 25 000× error in the direction that empties a card (visa-shop.ts:155-158). Also WHOLE đồng only (display-honesty: cards render `group(Math.round(price))`), and MAX_PRICE_VND = 2_000_000_000 is mirrored in fx.ts:108 — keep the two equal.

Lookups fail SOFT (null / []) but every consumer fails CLOSED. That means a transient DB error in the seller/listing lookup (swallowed at visa-shop.ts:256-259, :361-364) presents as `shop_unavailable` / `product_not_selected` / `product_price_unavailable`, never as a guessed price. Do not 'improve' resolveVisaProduct by giving it its own query — it re-reads the catalogue precisely so storefront-ownership, for-sale and sellable-price rules cannot be bypassed (visa-shop.ts:436-442). Likewise don't widen `isVisaShopListing` into a charging check (visa-shop.ts:485-494).

The hidden generic anchor is status='hidden' + price 0 by design, looked up by externalId over the RAW list (visa-shop.ts:496-508). It must never resolve as a product. A generic (product-less) start binds to it and gets the PICKER, not step 1 (dm-flow.ts:672-687, :1175-1180), and a resumed selection-less case retargets the thread header back to the anchor so no unchosen price appears in the header (dm-flow.ts:1193-1201).

metaJson may hold ids, step numbers, ONE money amount and payload FIELD NAMES — never a value the applicant typed (prisma/schema.prisma:635-640; dm-flow.ts:61-66, :107-118, :296-310). Corollary in errors and logs: refusals name KEYS only, zod errors are rebuilt from `issue.path` never `issue.message` (dm-flow.ts:598-605), and driver errors are never echoed (visaDmFailureFor, dm-flow.ts:214-235).

The money guard lives IN the SQL predicate, not in JS: writeVisaPayload's update carries `.in('status', EDITABLE)`, `.eq('updated_at', expected)` (CAS) AND `.is('paid_at', null)` — dm-flow.ts:531-540, with the comment 'the JS-side paid_at check is advisory; a payment capture that lands between our read and this write must void the write'. A 0-row miss returns `application_changed_retry` and must never be swallowed. Selection columns must ride the SAME CAS write via `extraSet` (dm-flow.ts:508-517, :1284-1291) — two updates invalidate each other's token.

`estimatedExpenses` (visa/schema.ts:61) IS a client-supplied number inside the encrypted payload — but it is a government-form trip-budget declaration and is referenced by no pricing or charging code. Don't mistake it for a fee, and don't wire it to one.

`usdToCentsExact` (visa-shop.ts:189-194) is still exported but MUST NOT be used to price a listing (:172-178) — nothing in the catalogue calls it; đồng→cents goes through fx.ts directly. Also `visaPaymentsConfig().feeCents` is only the dormant/live switch and prices NOTHING (applications/route.ts:32-37, dm-thread.ts:429-438); it must never cross to a client.

Provider amounts are trusted only against local truth: markVisaPaidAndHandoff refuses when `input.amountCents < paymentRow.amount_cents` or the currency differs (payments.ts:607) — `visa_payments.amount_cents` / `currency: 'USD'` are written at checkout (checkout/route.ts:303-311) and the comment there warns that neither a mid-checkout admin price edit nor an FX move may raise or lower it. Never write '₫' into that currency column.

prisma/schema.prisma:632's kind comment is STALE — it lists 4 kinds while src/lib/messages.ts:28 declares 6 ('visa_result', 'visa_picker' missing). Trust messages.ts (it is the write-time validator); a port that derives the card-kind union from the Prisma comment loses the picker and result cards.

findings.question: 1. How are message kinds declared/typed in src/lib/messages.ts? List every existing kind. Where would two new ones be added, and what else keys off the kind?
findings.answer:
Declaration is a frozen tuple + derived union, plus a SECOND narrower union for "card" kinds:

```ts
// src/lib/messages.ts:28-32
export const MESSAGE_KINDS = ['text', 'offer', 'visa_step', 'visa_checkout', 'visa_result', 'visa_picker'] as const
export type MessageKind = (typeof MESSAGE_KINDS)[number]
export type VisaCardKind = 'visa_step' | 'visa_checkout' | 'visa_result' | 'visa_picker'
const VISA_CARD_KINDS = new Set<string>(['visa_step', 'visa_checkout', 'visa_result', 'visa_picker'])
export const isVisaCardKind = (kind: string): kind is VisaCardKind => VISA_CARD_KINDS.has(kind)
```

Six kinds exist today: `text`, `offer`, `visa_step`, `visa_checkout`, `visa_result`, `visa_picker` (documented one-per-line at messages.ts:22-27). The DB column is plain TEXT with `@default("text")` (prisma/schema.prisma:632) — never an enum — so a new kind is an additive code change, no DDL.

WHERE TO ADD (in order, all in src/lib/messages.ts):
1. `MESSAGE_KINDS` at :28 (mandatory — the runtime guard at :312 throws `message_kind_invalid` otherwise) and the doc block :22-27.
2. If the kinds carry a structured payload: a `type XMeta = { v: 1, ... }` next to VisaStepMeta/VisaCheckoutMeta/VisaResultMeta/VisaPickerMeta (:41-82), then add them to the `MessageMeta` union at :83.
3. A strict zod schema next to visaStepMetaSchema/visaCheckoutMetaSchema/visaResultMetaSchema/visaPickerMetaSchema (:106-151), then a row in `META_SCHEMAS` (:153-158).
4. ⚠️ `META_SCHEMAS` is typed `Record<VisaCardKind, z.ZodType>` and `metaSchemaFor` (:159) takes `VisaCardKind`, and `parseMessageMeta` (:168-176) begins `if (!metaJson || !isVisaCardKind(kind)) return null`. So metaJson is READABLE only for kinds in `VISA_CARD_KINDS`. Adding a card kind that is NOT a visa card requires splitting that concept in two — see gotchas.

WHAT ELSE KEYS OFF `kind` inside this file:
- `insertMessage` :310 (`opts?.kind ?? 'text'`), :312 allowlist guard, :313 `isOffer`, :314 `isCard = isVisaCardKind(kind)`, :317 `if (opts?.meta && !isCard) throw new Error('message_meta_not_allowed')`, :318 `buildCardMeta` (visa-only authorship gates), :323 empty-body→`preview` substitution for cards only, :330-332 offerAmount/offerStatus/metaJson columns, :370 the "supersede pending offers" updateMany `kind:'offer'`, :390 `if (recipientId && isOffer)` — cards deliberately produce NO bell/push (:383-388).
- `buildCardMeta` :250-293: (1) only `convo.sellerProfileId === senderId` may author (:252), (2) the card's applicationId must match the thread's visa binding (:277-286), (3) `kind === 'visa_checkout' && status==='paid'` refused (:289), (4) 4096-byte cap (:291).
- `MESSAGE_ROW_SELECT` :179-182 (carries `kind` + `metaJson`, so every reader gets them) and `SerializedMessage` :184-188 (`kind: string`, `meta: MessageMeta | null`).
- Per-kind mutators, each pinned to one kind in its WHERE: `setVisaStepState` :443-447 (`kind:'visa_step'`), `setVisaPickerState` :473-476 (`kind:'visa_picker'`), `setVisaCheckoutStatus` :519-521 (`kind:'visa_checkout'`), `actOnOffer` :546-548 (`kind:'offer'`).

findings.question: 2. Show every place that tests kind and whether any of them make the `!m.kind` mistake.
findings.answer:
NOBODY currently makes the mistake. The single `!kind` test in the repo is correct and carries the post-mortem:

```ts
// src/hooks/use-chat-translation.ts:58-65
// ⚠️ `kind === 'text'` must be accepted explicitly. `Message.kind` is `@default("text")` in
// the schema and the conversation serializer sends it verbatim, so EVERY real message from
// the API carries kind:'text' — the original `!m.kind` test was true only for optimistic
// client rows, which are always `mine`. That one predicate silently made the whole feature
// a no-op: nothing was ever translatable. Undefined is still allowed for local rows.
function isTranslatable(m: ChatMsg): boolean {
  const plain = !m.kind || m.kind === 'text'
  return !m.mine && plain && !!m.body.trim() && !m.pending && !m.failed
}
```
The `!m.kind` half is deliberate and still needed: optimistic/realtime client rows genuinely have no kind (`Msg.kind?: string` at src/app/messages/[id]/page.tsx:168; the realtime-append literal at :332 omits kind and meta).

All four live in ONE 2329-line module: src/components/marketplace/visa-cards.tsx.

Components (props type → component):
- `VisaStepCardProps` :1237-1250 → `VisaStepCard` :1259 — `{ meta: VisaStepCardMeta; info: VisaThreadInfo | null; kase: VisaCase | null; caseError?: string | null; live: boolean; busy: boolean; onAct: (action:'acknowledge'|'skip'|'edit', fields?: Record<string,string>) => boolean | Promise<boolean>; onUpload: (kind: DocKind, file: File) => void | Promise<void> }` (onAct resolving TRUE is what closes the editor).
- `VisaCheckoutCardProps` :1682-1690 → `VisaCheckoutCard` :1701 — `{ meta: VisaCheckoutCardMeta; info; kase; live; busy; onPay: (provider:'stripe'|'paypal', quote: VisaQuoteWire) => void | Promise<void> }`.
- `VisaResultCardProps` :1890-1893 → `VisaResultCard` :1916 — `{ meta: VisaResultCardMeta; info }` only; no `live` ("it is never a prompt and never expires").
- `VisaPickerCardProps` :2240-2247 → `VisaPickerCard` :2249 — `{ meta: VisaPickerCardMeta; info; live; busy; onSelect: (listingId: string) => boolean | Promise<boolean> }`.

So the house shape is: `{ meta, info, live, busy, on<Verb> }` (+ `kase`/`caseError` when the card needs the case), with every action callback returning `boolean | Promise<boolean>` so the card only commits its UI on a server-accepted true.

The shared chrome is `CardShell` :1102-1133 (module-private): `{ step: VisaDmStep | null; title: string; tone?: 'live' | 'settled'; children; className }` — renders `w-[92%] max-w-md rounded-2xl border px-3.5 py-3`, `tone==='live' ? 'border-brand/30 bg-card shadow-pop' : 'border-border bg-card/70'`, a Sparkles + "e-Visa" eyebrow, an optional `Step N of 5` Badge, and an `h3` title. `StepDots` :1138 is the 5-dot rail. A new card family should either reuse `CardShell` (export it) or clone this shape.

Meta parsers, one per kind, all with the identical fail-closed first line:
- `parseVisaStepMeta` :142 — `if (kind !== 'visa_step' || !isRecord(value)) return null`
- `parseVisaCheckoutMeta` :157, `parseVisaPickerMeta` :175, `parseVisaResultMeta` :203 (which also re-checks the reference against `/^EV-[1-9][0-9]{0,17}$/` rather than trusting the server).
- `parseVisaThreadInfo` :222 turns the thread's `visa` blob into `VisaThreadInfo` (mode · product · quote · providers, type at :98-116).
These are STRUCTURAL client-side re-validation on top of the server's strict zod (messages.ts:168) — copy that discipline: the client renders no live prompt off a blob it cannot read.

gotchas: THE BIG ONE: `isVisaCardKind` does DOUBLE DUTY — it means both "has metaJson" and "is subject to the visa authorship gates". `insertMessage` :314-318 does `const isCard = isVisaCardKind(kind)`; `if (opts?.meta && !isCard) throw new Error('message_meta_not_allowed')`; `const card = isCard ? await buildCardMeta(...)`. So if your two new kinds are NOT visa cards: (a) passing `meta` throws `message_meta_not_allowed`, and (b) adding them to VISA_CARD_KINDS to fix that instead subjects them to buildCardMeta, which requires `convo.sellerProfileId === senderId` (:252) AND a matching `visa_applications` binding (:277-286) — a non-visa thread has neither, so every send throws `visa_card_application_mismatch`. Correct port: split the concept (e.g. `CARD_KINDS`/`isCardKind` for metaJson eligibility vs `isVisaCardKind` for the visa gates), and widen `META_SCHEMAS`/`metaSchemaFor`/`parseMessageMeta` (:153-176) off `VisaCardKind`.

`parseMessageMeta` (src/lib/messages.ts:168-169) returns null for any kind not in VISA_CARD_KINDS. Forget that and your metaJson round-trips as `meta: null` from src/app/api/conversations/[id]/route.ts:235 — the card renders as an inert bubble with no error anywhere. Fails SILENTLY.
Adding the kind to `MESSAGE_KINDS` (:28) is mandatory: the runtime guard at :312 throws `message_kind_invalid` for anything else, and it runs before any card logic.

CARDS MUST BE SENT WITH AN EMPTY BODY + `opts.preview`. The realtime broadcast payload carries only (id, senderProfileId, body, createdAt) — no kind, no meta (messages.ts:295-307). The thread client refetches only when the broadcast body is EMPTY (`if (!p.id || !p.body) { load(); return }`, page.tsx:324); a non-empty body instead appends a plain text bubble via the literal at page.tsx:332 that has NO kind/meta, so your card renders as a raw text bubble until the 15s backstop poll. Note the extra escape hatch at :327 — bodies starting with 💰/✅/❌ also force a refetch.

`preview` PERSISTS into `Conversation.lastMessageText` (messages.ts:340), a plaintext column BOTH parties' inboxes read, and tr() cannot run at render time there. It must be a bilingual composite string (the idiom: `'Chọn dịch vụ e-Visa · Choose your e-Visa service'`, dm-thread.ts:415) and must contain no user/applicant data.

Add the new kinds to the unreadable-meta fallback predicate at page.tsx:1212. Its whole purpose is that a card body is empty by design, so a card whose meta this build can't parse must not fall through to the empty default bubble at :1225.

Cards deliberately get NO bell notification and NO push — `if (recipientId && isOffer)` at messages.ts:390, reasoned at :383-388. If your new kinds should notify, that is a deliberate change to that gate, not an oversight to 'fix' silently.

Empty-body cards leak blank lines into two admin surfaces that only special-case 'offer': src/app/admin/conversation/[id]/page.tsx:90 (renders `m.body` → empty bubble) and src/app/api/admin/ai-review/route.ts:285-289 (emits `Buyer: ` with nothing after it into the AI prompt). Add a branch in both if the card matters to moderation/AI review.

Live-translation exclusion is automatic but check the direction you want: `isTranslatable` = `!m.kind || m.kind === 'text'` (src/hooks/use-chat-translation.ts:64), so a new kind is never translated. If your card carries real prose in `body`, it will silently NOT be translated. Also do NOT 'simplify' that predicate to `!m.kind` — the comment at :58-63 records that exact bug making the whole feature a no-op.

Every actionable card kind needs its own act route (or a widened predicate): src/app/api/visa/cards/[messageId]/act/route.ts:77 hard-refuses `row.kind !== 'visa_step'` with 404. Copy its gate stack: 401 (:49) → shape (:57-68) → kind (:77) → `buyerProfileId !== userId` → 403 not_your_card (:80) → re-parse meta (:84) → superseded → 409 (:86).

The ordinary send route CANNOT author cards, by design: src/app/api/conversations/[id]/messages/route.ts:87-92 builds the ConvoForSend literal without `visaApplicationId` and passes only `{kind:'offer'}` or undefined. Don't 'fix' it by piping a client-supplied kind/meta through — messages.ts:245-249 explicitly declines to rely on that absence, and the four gates exist precisely because a client-forwarded kind must stay impossible.

If a new kind needs at-most-one-per-thing, the precedent is a PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX applied out-of-band, not Prisma: scripts/visa-result-card-unique.mjs (`where kind = 'visa_result'`), and result.ts:316-325 treats the losing insert's throw as the race decider. Prisma schema has no unique on Message.

prisma/schema.prisma:626-632 is ALREADY STALE — the comment and the `// 'text' | 'offer' | 'visa_step' | 'visa_checkout'` inline list omit visa_result and visa_picker. Update both the schema comment and the messages.ts:22-27 block, or the next reader will believe there are four kinds.

Every new metaJson field is a PII surface with a hard rule: metaJson must carry ids, small numbers, and payload FIELD NAMES only (messages.ts:34-38, prisma/schema.prisma:636-640). The existing schemas enforce it structurally — uuid regexes, `needsReview` restricted to `Object.keys(visaPayloadSchema.shape)` (:89, :112), `amountUsd` bounded to money (:122), `reference` accepted only if `normalizeVisaReference(v) === v` (:135), `.strict()` everywhere, 4096-byte cap (:101). Any free-form string you add is the hole external review already flagged twice.

Every write of metaJson — insert AND update — must pass a strict re-parse of the RESULT, never trust the caller's value: setVisaStepState :454, setVisaPickerState :479, setVisaCheckoutStatus :528. Mirror that in any new mutator.

Card visibility/actionability is derived client-side by a reverse-scan memo, not by a DB flag (page.tsx:910-946). Any new actionable kind needs one, or every historical card in the thread renders as a live prompt. Note the asymmetry to preserve: step + picker are silenced by `visaInfo.mode === 'admin'`, checkout deliberately is NOT (:935-937).
